rows.jyutping: jau6 daai6 fung1 jau6 daai6 jyu5
rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken choice for stormy weather, especially when both the wind and rain are strong.

example.english: It’s stormy today, so don’t go out.
example.traditional: 今日又大風又大雨，唔好出街喇。
example.jyutping: gam1 jat6 jau6 daai6 fung1 jau6 daai6 jyu5 m4 hou2 ceot1 gaai1 laa3

rows.note: Use this for stormy passions or violent, rough conflicts rather than for the weather or a generally troubled relationship.

example.jyutping: keoi5 dei6 ge3 zaang1 leon6 hou2 gik1 lit6

rows.note: Use this for a stormy relationship or other troubled interpersonal situation marked by tension and quarrelling.

example.english: My relationship with them is stormy right now.
example.traditional: 我同佢嘅關係而家好緊張。
example.jyutping: ngo5 tung4 keoi5 ge3 gwaan1 hai6 ji4 gaa1 hou2 gan2 zoeng1

rows.note: Use this productive construction when stormy means related to storms rather than describing stormy weather itself.

example.english: This report has lots of information related to stormy weather.
example.traditional: 呢份報告有好多同風暴有關嘅資料。
example.jyutping: ni1 fan6 bou3 gou3 jau5 hou2 do1 tung4 fung1 bou6 jau5 gwaan1 ge3 zi1 liu2
